title: Flow-matching losses and velocity targets
hook: The target for each training pair is simple. Why the loss never reaches zero, why the same error looks different in other units, and what ComfyUI's own trainer really minimises.

verified.claim: CONST mixes as sigma * noise + (1 - sigma) * latent and reads the clean estimate as x - sigma * output.
TrainSampler compares the model's clean estimate with the latent, using a loss chosen from MSE, L1, Huber and SmoothL1.
TrainSampler draws sigma with percent_to_sigma of a uniform number.
Least squares on the per-pair target has identical gradients to least squares on the marginal field.
verified.ref: Lipman et al. 2022, Theorem 2, as stated in CU-204

verified.claim: Esser et al. describe logit-normal timestep sampling with parameters m and s, and rf/lognorm(0.00, 1.00) ranks first in their table.
The ratio of clean-latent loss to velocity loss is sigma squared, on a perfect model.

unchecked: The floors are for a one-dimensional mixture. A real model's floor is not known, and it depends on the data.

We read core's trainer and did not run a flow model through it for this lesson. That its weighting differs from any published recipe is arithmetic, and we have no result on whether it matters for pictures.
Whether a particular published trainer uses velocity loss is outside this lesson, since we did not read those trainers.
